Summary: The hilarious #1  New York Times  bestselling classic picture book about a chimpanzee in a very bad mood--perfect for young children learning how to deal with confusing feelings.    Jim the chimpanzee is in a terrible mood for no good reason. His friends can't understand it--how can he be in a bad mood when it's SUCH a beautiful day? They have lots of suggestions for how to make him feel better. But Jim can't take all the advice...and has a BIT of a meltdown. Could it be that he just needs a day to feel grumpy?  Suzanne and Max Lang bring hilarity and levity to this very important lesson on emotional literacy, demonstrating to kids that they are allowed to feel their feelings. Grumpy Monkey  is the first title in a series of books targeted at different ages that encourage kids to feel their feelings.
Customer Reviews (Text): Customers love this children's book for its adorable illustrations and how it helps children understand and identify their emotions. Moreover, the book is great for all ages, making it a favorite bedtime read, and customers appreciate its humor, with one noting the physical humor in the pictures. Additionally, customers find the book helpful in teaching children it's okay to sometimes feel grumpy, and one review highlights how Suzanne Lang effectively compares emotional experiences.

Book Title: We Don't Eat Our Classmates: A Penelope Rex Book
Author: Ryan Higgins
Categories (Amazon): Books > Children's Books > Growing Up & Facts of Life > Friendship, Social Skills & School Life > School
Summary: It's the first day of school for Penelope Rex, and she can't wait to meet her classmates . But it's hard to make human friends when they're so darn delicious! That is, until Penelope gets a taste of her own medicine and finds she may not be at the top of the food chain after all. . . . Readers will gobble up this hilarious new story from award-winning author-illustrator Ryan T. Higgins.

Customers praise its educational value, serving as a great introduction to school and teaching important lessons about being kind and thinking of others' feelings. The book appeals to children of various elementary ages.
